summary: Compact UUID truncation in client idempotency header causes duplicate executions for batched multi-tool requests
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports duplicates of downstream side-effects (jobs created in their system) when sending batched multi-tool/function-calling requests from our SDKs. The customer uses a pattern where a single request contains multiple per-action tool invocations (e.g. external HTTP webhook calls and internal DB updates).

Impact: Repeated downstream job creation in production for ~18 customers in the same BrightLane org. Customer reports >20 duplicate jobs per 1k requests during a traffic spike. Business impact: clinical scheduling jobs duplicated, causing confusion and manual reconciliation.

Environment: BrightLane uses Redwood SDKs in a Node + Python mixed service. SDK versions reported: python 1.8.3, go 1.4.6, ts 2.2.0. All traffic flows through a customer edge proxy and our API Gateway in us-east (prod).

Observed behaviour: When batching 3-5 tool calls in a single request, sometimes one of the per-action idempotency keys is treated as a different key server-side and the tool is executed again on retry/failover. This seems correlated to high concurrency and when requests are routed through an older edge proxy instance.

Expected behaviour: Each per-action idempotency token should be treated atomically and deduplicated server-side regardless of header encoding or transport layer optimizations.

Attachments: customer provided request traces, sample encoded headers, and downstream job IDs (attached in ticket).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use SDK to send a batched multi-tool request with per-action idempotency keys (UUID v4).
2) Simulate intermittent network by killing the connection and reconnecting (or send in high concurrency).
3) Allow SDK to retry according to default policy.
4) Observe duplicate downstream jobs when the per-action idempotency key is interpreted differently by the server during retry resolution.

investigation_notes:
Initial triage: duplicates only occur for per-action keys that have been compacted/truncated by upstream proxy. Server-side dedupe logic treats canonical hyphenated uuid and compacted base36 string as different keys.
Hypothesis: two failure modes: (1) client-side or proxy-side header normalization/truncation results in key variants, (2) dedupe index uses raw header string instead of a stable canonicalized id.
Evidence: proxy logs show base36/truncated values for Idempotency-Action headers arriving at gateway instance A, while retry attempt arriving at gateway instance B carried full hyphenated uuid. Dedup store lookup uses exact-match on header value.
Repro on staging: reproduced by injecting header-transforming proxy; when transform applied, dedupe missed and duplicate executions observed.
Risk: medium-high for any customers using edge proxies that rewrite headers. Affects batched per-action idempotency patterns and can surface as duplicated downstream work.
resolution_notes:
Workarounds provided to customer: 1) disable header compaction plugin in their edge proxy (confirmed reduced duplicates), 2) configure SDKs to attach an additional canonical header 'Idempotency-Action-Canonical' that contains the lowercase hyphenated UUID (SDK PRs in progress).
Planned fixes: server-side normalization to canonical UUID on dedupe lookup (ENG-issue linked in related_github_prs). SDKs (python/go/ts) to perform idempotency header canonicalization and to emit both compact and canonical forms for backward compatibility.
Deployment plan: server normalization to be rolled out behind a feature flag in us-east on 2026-03-18, SDK releases to follow (python 1.8.4, go 1.4.7). Post-deploy: monitor duplicate rate for BrightLane and global customers for two weeks.
Follow-ups: update public SDK docs with explicit guidance on idempotency header formats and a decoupled section about upstream header rewrites; create a runbook for this class of dedupe failures.
